extraction.name: MathQA
extraction.description: A large-scale, diverse dataset of 37k English multiple-choice math word problems covering multiple math domain categories, annotated with fully-specified operational programs using a domain-aware representation language.
extraction.creator: Aida Amini, Saadia Gabriel, Shanchuan Lin, Rik Koncel-Kedziorski, Yejin Choi, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Problems were sourced from the AQuA dataset, categorized into math domains using term frequencies, and densely annotated with formal operation programs via crowdsourcing using a dynamic annotation platform.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Unsolvable problems (e.g., sequence problems, problems requiring brute-force/options, non-numeric problems, problems without words) and duplicates were filtered or removed. Annotations were expanded by finding closely similar problems using Levenshtein distance (threshold of 4 words in edit distance) and replacing numeric values with generic numbers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdsourced annotators iteratively selected operations and arguments using a dynamic annotation platform providing hints/formulas and intermediate calculated results. Restrictions required the program to include numbers from the problem and produce a final calculation very close to the correct numeric solution. Pre-defined test questions were used for quality control, requiring annotators to maintain an accuracy threshold.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Alignment validation required at least 2 out of 3 validators to rank an operation program as valid, yielding 94.64% validation accuracy across categories. Expert evaluation of 500 problems showed 92% validity and 87% agreement between expert validation and the crowdsourcing validation task.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note statistical bias in datasets like AQuA, which their representation language provides an extra layer of supervision to reduce.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Omits high-order polynomials and problems where solutions are entirely nonnumeric. Categorization strategy can be noisy due to polysemous n-grams. Does not cover operations like factorization or problem domains like sequences and logic.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of interpretable neural math problem solvers and sequence-to-program models.
